text: William John Miller II (September 17, 1979 – September 15, 2023) was an American actor known for his work on American soap operas, including his award-winning performance as Billy Abbott on The Young and the Restless and his dual portrayals of Jason Morgan and Drew Cain on General Hospital. Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, he grew up in Grand Prairie, Texas, and spent five years as a patient at the Texas Scottish Rite Hospital for Children, an organization he also supported. He attended Lamar High School in Arlington, Texas, and earned a communications degree from the University of Texas in Austin, where he was one of only twenty students in the film department's intensive Production Sequence. After graduating, Miller moved to Los Angeles and began working in the mail room at Industry Entertainment. His first acting break came after signing with the Wilhelmina modeling agency, during which he appeared in six commercials, including two for Electronic Arts' The Sims, as well as for JCPenney, Pizza Hut, and pokerparty.com. At age 24, he screen-tested for As the World Turns on CBS, lost the audition citing bad management, and subsequently left his agency and management company, taking a two-year hiatus from acting. In 2006, he returned to acting with a role in an episode of CSI: NY, followed by a role as Richie Novak, the murdering and blackmailing brother of Annie Lavery, on All My Children, beginning August 30, 2007. After the character's demise in August 2008, Miller resumed auditioning, with key involvement from Barbara Bloom, Julie Hanan Carruthers, Marla Kanelos, Peter Bergman, and Elizabeth Hendrickson, leading to his casting as Billy Abbott on The Young and the Restless. Miller submitted the longest Emmy reel among all nominated performers—over 32 minutes long, equivalent to an entire episode—and was awarded Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series on June 27, 2010 and June 14, 2013. In 2011, he received a second nomination in the same category for his role as Billy Abbott. He also appeared as himself in the independent film Remembering Nigel, which premiered at the Paso Robles Digital Film Festival on November 25, 2009. In August 2012, he joined The CW's Ringer as a recurring cast member, and in 2013, he was cast as Gabe Watson in the Lifetime made-for-TV movie Fatal Honeymoon. In November 2013, it was announced he would depart the role of Billy Abbott, with David Tom named as his successor; Miller described the decision as the "hardest thing" he had ever done. On September 2, 2014, General Hospital executive producer Frank Valentini announced Miller would join the cast as Jason Morgan. In March 2018, he earned a nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor for his portrayal of Jason Morgan. In 2017, with Steve Burton's return to the role of Jason, Miller's casting was retconned to that of his twin, Drew Cain. In July 2019, Miller announced his exit from the soap. Miller died in Austin, Texas, on September 15, 2023. In a statement, his mother Patricia revealed his death was due to suicide following years of battling bipolar depression: "He fought a long hard valiant battle with bipolar depression for years. He did everything he could to control the disease. He loved his family, his friends and his fans but in the end the disease won the fight and he surrendered his life." The final autopsy report, conducted in November 2023 and released in December 2023, concluded that Miller's death was a suicide resulting from a "gunshot wound of the head." Toxicology reports found the presence of "ethanol, cocaine, and its metabolites, diphenhydramine, and amphetamine." The report noted Miller was found with an apparent gunshot wound to the head, multiple letters indicating suicidal intent and instructions for others were discovered at the scene, and a revolver chambered for .410 shotgun shells was found in his right hand.
